landManager: National Park Service
storedPass: Mount Rainier NP entrance pass (covered by park entrance fee / America the Beautiful pass) — Northwest Forest Pass does not apply inside the park
drive: Enter Mount Rainier National Park at the Nisqually entrance and, after 1 mile, turn left (north) onto Westside Road. Drive it to the Dry Creek barricade and park in the small lot just south of it; past the barricade the road is closed to vehicles.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness, with some upper routes crossing into North Cascades National Park
storedPass: None required at the Nooksack Cirque Trailhead; a Northwest Forest Pass is required at many other trailheads in the area.
Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From the Nooksack Cirque Trailhead at the end of FR-34 off Hannegan Pass Road (FR-32); Ruth Creek has no bridge at the trailhead

names: Cedar Creek Trailhead (Sandy Butte-Cedar Creek Road #200)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District; Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass
Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From Winthrop, drive SR-20 west 17 miles, then turn south onto FR-200 at the signed turn and go 0.8 mile to the trailhead.

names: Pacific Crest Trail Trailhead (Snoqualmie Pass, Red Mountain #1033)
SR-20 pullout near milepost 165-166 (Silver Star / Wine Spires)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
None currently required
drive: From the broad SR-20 pullout near milepost 165-166 (~4 miles east of Washington Pass)

landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: From Port Angeles up Hurricane Ridge Road (NPS entrance fee), then ~2 miles on the unpaved Obstruction Point Road to where the road passes directly beneath Steeple Rock

names: Snow Lake Trailhead (Stevens Canyon Road, Mount Rainier NP)
landManager: National Park Service — Mount Rainier National Park
storedPass: Standard Mount Rainier NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7 days), $55 Mount Rainier annual pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
Mount Rainier National Park entrance pass or America the Beautiful interagency pass.
drive: From the Snow Lake Trailhead on Stevens Canyon Road (~4,500 ft); Stevens Canyon Road closes in winter — winter parties typically start from Narada Falls

landManager: White River National Forest - Maroon Bells-Snowmass Wilderness
storedPass: Parking pass required

names: Bradley Pond Trailhead (Santanoni Range), Upper Works Road

landManager: Wallowa-Whitman National Forest (Eagle Cap Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest / Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass, day pass or Interagency pass to park at the Wolf Creek trailhead
Northwest Forest Pass required at the Wolf Creek Trailhead — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From Winthrop, take Twin Lakes Road and Wolf Creek Road, then a gravel Forest Service road to its end at the Wolf Creek Trailhead (about 3,000 ft).

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest — Alpine Lakes Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($5/day or $30/annual) at the Teanaway/Ingalls Creek trailheads.
drive: From the Beverly Turnpike Trailhead at the end of FR-9737-112 (~3,650 ft) off the North Fork Teanaway River Road, via Trail #1391 up Beverly Creek

landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: No day-use pass; a paid/reserved backcountry permit is required for any overnight stay (see fees).
drive: From Newhalem, follow SR-20 east to milepost 130 at Diablo Lake, then enter the south side of Colonial Creek Campground and park in the large lot above the boat ramp.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Snoqualmie Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass ($30/yr) or America the Beautiful pass, or a $5/day pass at developed trailheads.
drive: From I-90 Exit 47 (Denny Creek and Tinkham Road), turn left over the freeway, then 0.2 mile ahead turn right onto FR 58. Pass under the freeway, turn left after 0.2 mile, and continue 2.9 miles; the parking lots are on the right, about half a mile beyond Denny Creek Campground.
From the Pullman-Moscow Highway, turn off at the stoplight onto Terre View Drive and park off it. Check whether a parking permit applies where you pull off.

names: Cutthroat Peak Climbers Trail Pullout (Hwy 20, ~1.5 mi W of Washington Pass, north side)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: Drive SR-20 to Washington Pass and continue west about 1.5 miles to a long, wide pullout beside the highway, which is the climbers' parking. SR-20 closes for winter.
From US 2 at Leavenworth, drive up Icicle Creek Road to the Bridge Creek Campground junction, which is where the road ends in winter.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Cle Elum Ranger District, within the Alpine Lakes Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / America the Beautiful Interagency Pass
Northwest Forest Pass

names: SR-20 turnout below Le Petit Cheval (east of Washington Pass)
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From the SR-20 turnout below Le Petit Cheval: unmarked cairned climbers' trail across Early Winters Creek and up the drainage to the formation

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Wenatchee River Ranger District (Henry M. Jackson Wilderness)
storedPass: None confirmed required (verify current signage)
None
drive: From Leavenworth, drive US 2 west about 31 miles, turn right onto Smithbrook Road (Forest Road 6700) and go about 3 miles to the trailhead on the left. Forest Road 6700 is closed to vehicles by a storm-damage order from May 20, 2026 through December 31, 2027, unless lifted sooner.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest / Mount Baker Ranger District; lower approach crosses private timber/Olivine Corp land.
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / National Park Pass
drive: The Elbow Lake trailhead is about 11 miles up Forest Road 38 off Mosquito Lake Road, and the road past mile 9 is closed each year from December 1 to June 15. Since July 2026 Forest Road 38 has been closed to vehicles by a washout at milepost 7.

landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
Northwest Forest Pass
drive: From Glacier, drive SR-542 about 23 miles toward Austin Pass; the Lake Ann trailhead is on the right in a paved lot just below Artist Point.

landManager: USDA Forest Service — Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Mt. Baker National Recreation Area
storedPass: NW Forest Pass
Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
drive: From Burlington, take I-5 exit 230 and drive SR-20 east about 23 miles, turn left onto Baker Lake Road 0.4 miles past milepost 82 and follow it 12.3 miles, turn left onto Forest Road 12 for 3.7 miles, then right onto Forest Road 13 for 5.3 miles to the trailhead parking.

landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District / Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / Interagency Recreation Pass / Digital Day Pass
Northwest Forest Pass, interagency pass, or day-use fee at Crater Creek Trailhead
drive: Drive to the Crater Creek Trailhead (4,750 ft): from Twisp, take WA-20 east 2 miles to WA-153, then south 12 miles to County Rd 1029/1034 (signed for Foggy Dew Campground) and follow it about 6 miles as it becomes FR 4340 - pavement ends around mile 4 (bear right) - then continue on FR 4340-300 roughly 4.6 more miles to the trailhead parking area (vault toilet, stock ramp, no potable water).

landManager: National Park Service — Olympic National Park (Olympic Wilderness)
storedPass: Olympic NP entrance fee: $30/vehicle (7-day), $55 annual Olympic NP pass, or $80 America the Beautiful interagency annual pass.
drive: Via the Elwha Valley: Olympic Hot Springs Road is closed to vehicles at Madison Falls — walk or bike ~6.2 miles to the Whiskey Bend Trailhead
